Efficient whole-cell biosynthesis of (S)-2-chloro-1-(3,4-difluorophenyl)-ethanol from 2-chloro-1-(3,4-difluoro- phenyl) ethanone in a sustainable reaction system
Linghui Kong ¹, Bo Fan ¹, Yu-Cai He *
School of Pharmacy & School of Biological and Food Engineering, Changzhou University, Changzhou 213164, China
ARTICLE INFO --- Keywords: (S)-2-Chloro-1-(3,4-difluorophenyl)-ethanol 2-Chloro-1-(3,4-difluorophenyl) ethanone Asymmetric bioreduction Reductase Deep eutectic solvent

ABSTRACT (S)-2-Chloro-1-(3,4-difluorophenyl)-ethanol [(S)-CFPL] is a key chiral intermediate in the manufacture of Ticagrelor. In this study, deep eutectic solvent (DES) was used as the co-solvent, and several reaction parameters were investigated and characterized. It was observed that supplementary of DES could promote the asymmetric reduction of 2-chloro-1-(3,4-difluorophenyl) ethanone (CFPO) to (S)-CFPL through the biological reduction by recombinant E. coli containing a NADH-dependent reductase CmCR. The high pKa value of carboxylic acid in DES and low viscosity of DES were beneficial to increase cell membrane permeability and enhancement of biocatalytic efficiency. By supplementary of DES ChCl:LA (7.5 vol%) into the bioreaction system, the efficient bioreduction reaction of 100 mM CFPO was achieved via the biocatalysis with whole-cell at 30 °C and pH 7.0, affording (S)-CFPL in 95.9% yield and optical purity > 99 %. The process was environmentally friendly with high biocatalytic productivity and had potential practicability in the mass production of (S)-CFPL.

## 1. Introduction Optically active chiral alcohols have received a lot of attention due to their relatively stable molecular structure and their potential as key building-block in the manufacture of materials, pesticides and various compounds used in pharmaceuticals [1]. For example, (_S_)-1-(2, 6-dichloro-3-fluorophenyl) ethanol is an important intermediate for Crizotinib [2]. Other chiral alcohols are also important intermediates of Duloxetine [3], Aprepitant [4], and Sitagliptin [5], as shown in Fig. 1. Chiral compounds are now synthesized by biocatalysts [6-8]. Compared with chemical catalysis, biocatalysis has the characteristics of high ef- ficiency [9,10], specificity [11,12], gentleness [13] and adjustable ac- tivity [14]. Ticagrelor is a platelet aggregation inhibitor primarily used in acute coronary syndromes [15], and (_S_)-2-chloro-1-(3,4-difluor- ophonyl)-ethanol [(_S_)-CFPL] is a key chiral intermediate for preparing Ticagrelor. The chemical synthesis of (_S_)-CFPL involves the reduction of CFPO in organic solvents by chemocatalysts such as borane-methyl sulfide complex and chiral compounds [16]. Compared with bio- catalysis, traditional chemical reduction methods always involve a va- riety of expensive chiral catalysts and cumbersome post-treatment processes [17]. Therefore, the synthesis method of (_S_)-CFPL needs to be

further improved. Currently, two methods to synthesize chiral alcohols are commonly utilized via biocatalytic approach: dynamic kinetic res- olution and asymmetric bioreduction [18]. Han et al. identified an alcohol dehydrogenase from _Rhodococcus_ R6 that catalyzed the asym- metric transformation of 2-hydroxyacetophenone into (_R_)-(-)-1-phenyl-1,2-ethanediol [19]. Xia et al. obtained three optical compounds by developing a lipase from _Candida Antarctica_ that cata- lyzed the doubly enantioselective ring-opening decomposition between racemic alcohol and lactone [20]. Tozlu et al. used _Lactobacillus para-_ _casei_ BD101 as a biocatalyst for asymmetric reduction of (4-chlor- ophenyl)(phenyl) methane [21]. Chemical catalyst can cause major ecological problems in terms of high energy consumption and toxic waste formation. Biocatalysis has outstanding advantages over chemo- catalysis, including mild reaction conditions, high stereoselectivity and high catalytic efficiency [22]. Biocatalyst is one of the attractive tech- nology options to overcome the limitations of traditional catalysts in this field.

During the process of biocatalysis, reaction medium is very impor- tant to improve the biocatalytic efficiency [23]. More and more atten- tion has recently been paid to deep eutectic-solvents (DESs) in biocatalysis [24–26]. DES is commonly composed of

hydrogen-bond-donor (HBD) and hydrogen-bond-acceptor (HBA). Due to its good biocompatibility and high stability, it is considered as the most promising green solvent to replace ionic liquid and organic solvent [27]. DES synthesized from choline chloride is one of the many types of DESs, which could change the composition by adjusting different HBDs [28,29]. DESs have been widely utilized in the chemocatalysis and biocatalysis [30]. They have important physical properties such as viscosity, conductivity, and thermal stability [31–33]. In addition, the typical characteristics of DES in the process of biocatalytic reaction are as follows: (a) higher solubility for substrates with poor water solubility, which make the substrates more easily recognized and utilized by biocatalysts [34]; (b) improve the activity and stability of biocatalysts [35]; (c) reduce the occurrence of side reactions, which make the reaction more selective enantiomers [36]. DES may alter the viscosity of bioreaction medium, and the change in osmolality caused by the viscosity will influence the permeability of cell membrane. The enhanced permeability of bacterial cell membranes (by mutations in its structure) might lead to a significant improvement in whole-cell biocatalytic efficiency [37].

Distinct from the isolated enzymes, one of the main advantages of the whole-cell biocatalysts is that the whole cells provide an excellent natural environment for the enzymes, allow co-factors to regenerate, and avoid enzyme inactivation and denaturation that might occur under some harsh performance conditions [38–41]. The whole cell catalyst is also the cheapest catalyst formulation. DES is a new type of green, solvent with low volatility, high stability, good biocompatibility and other characteristics [33]. In this study, whole cells of recombinant E. coli containing a NADH-dependent reductase CmCR [42] were used for bioreduction of CFPO into (S)-CFPL by using the mixture of DES and H2O as reaction system. The relationship of pKa value of carboxylic acid in DES, viscosity of DES and biocatalytic activity was explored. The effects of DES as a co-solvent on cell viability and cell membrane permeability were also studied, and then the effects of DES on biotransformation were also examined. In addition, biological reaction parameters (such as reaction temperature, pH, co-substrate loading, cofactor loading, metal ion loading and biocatalyst loading) were investigated. Finally, a sustainable production strategy for biocatalytic synthesis of ticagrelor chiral intermediates (S)-CFPL was developed in a benign reaction system.
## 2. Materials and methods ### 2.1. Chemicals and materials CFPO was obtained from Aladdin Co., Ltd. (Shanghai, China). Choline chloride (ChCl), tartaric acid, malonic acid, citric acid, D,L-
malic acid, lactic acid, D-glucose, KH2PO4, K2HPO4, MgCl2, and other reagents were from Shanghai Lingfeng Chemical Reagent Co., Ltd. (China).

2.2. _Synthesis of DESs_ Equal molar of ChCl as HBA and organic acid (tartaric acid, malonic acid, citric acid, malic acid, and lactic acid) as HBD were supplemented to a 250-mL flask by stirring magnetically in an oil bath at 80 °C and heated for 2 h. ChCl:Tartaric acid (ChCl:TA), ChCl:Malonic acid (ChCl: MOA), ChCl:Citric acid (ChCl:CA), ChCl: Malic acid (ChCl:MA) and ChCl:Lactic acid (ChCl:LA), were used as cosolvent.

2.3. Determination of Kamlet-Taft parameters of DESs The measurement of Kamlet-Taft (K-T) parameters were determined, with N,N-dimethyl-4-nitroaniline as indices of π*, Nile red dye and 4-nitroaniline as indices of α and β, respectively. Dyes were prepared from anhydrous methanol solution, in which the concentrations of N,N-dimethyl-4-nitrobenzene, Nile red and 4-nitroaniline were all 1 mM. The dye solution (2 mL) was first transferred to a 5 mL centrifuge tube, then vacuum-dried at 40 °C for 5 h to remove the methanol. 3 mL DES was added to the test tube for dissolving the dye under the ultrasound (300 W) at 25 °C, and then transferred to a quartz colorimetric dish. Ultraviolet spectrophotometer (L6S, Shanghai INESA Scientific Instruments Co., Ltd) was applied to detect the absorption wavelength of the mixture in the wavelength range of 300–700 nm at room temperature. The solvatochromic parameters were calculated using the following equations:

## 2.5. Molecular docking Three kinds of E. coli containing carbonyl reductase CmCR [47], SsCR [39] and KpADH [40] were preserved in the laboratory, namely E. coli CCZU-K14, E. coli CCZU-SF21 and E. coli KpADH. The most suit- able enzyme was selected by molecular docking. CmCR was a model structure based on Genbank: BAE46987.1, built through a Swiss model server. SsCR was a NADPH-dependent carbonyl reductase (PDB: 1ZZE) from Sporospora salmoni. KpADH was a polysporous alcohol dehydro- genase (PDB: 5Z2X) of Kluyveromycetes. The substrate CFPO was con- nected to the model structure of CmCR, SsCR and KpADH via AutoDock Vina. For molecular docking, ligands and residues were set to be flexible and rigid, respectively. The size and center Settings of the grid box were as follows: CmCR: center x, y, z = 1.159, 0.37, -1.127, size x, y, z = 40, 40, 40; SsCR: center x, y, z = 3.546, 15.0, 19.997, size x, y, z = 40, 40, 40; KpADH: center x, y, z=-46.344, 123.84, -1.362, size x, y, z = 40, 40, 40. The docking run was conducted, and the substrate for docking with the direction of low energy production was selected for analysis.

2.6. Measurement of reductase activity The reductase activity was determined using 2.0 mM CFPO as substrate by monitoring the decrease in the absorbance of NADH at 340 nm. The reaction mixture used to determine reductase enzyme activity contained 2.95 mL buffer (potassium phosphate buffer, pH 7.0), 0.10 mM NADH, 2.0 mM CFPO and 50 µL crude enzyme (ultrasonic broken) in a total volume of 3.0 mL. One unit (U) of reductase activity was defined as the amount of enzyme catalyzing 1.0 µmol NADH per minute under these conditions.

2.7. Determination of membrane integrity The integrity of the cell membrane was assessed by EU-2200 UV spectrophotometer (Shanghai Onlab Instruments Co., Ltd) with absorbance values at 260 nm and 280 nm. The whole cells were completely suspended in the buffer solution and a certain amount of DES was added under 30 °C and 180 rpm for 8 h. The cloudy cell fluid was extracted, the cells were rotated and centrifuged, and the OD260 and OD280 values were determined. Three parallel controls were performed for each experiment.

The membrane integrity of the cells was measured by flow cytometry (FCM) and fluorescence microscopy (FL). 100 mg/mL of cells were incubated in the reaction media under 30 °C, pH 7.0 and 180 rpm for 8 h. Then it was diluted to 150 CFU/mL with PBS of pH 7.0, stained with 1 mL propidium iodide (PI) (50 µg/mL), and stored at 4 °C in the dark for 30 min. The integrity of the cell membrane was detected by flow cytometry (BD Accuri™ C6 Plus) with a wavelength of 488 nm and an emission wavelength of 630 nm. The cell morphology was observed by fluorescence microscope (Carl Zeiss, ZEN-3-0-blue-Hotfix-4) with magnification of 30 times.
2.8. Bioreduction of CFPO Recombinant _E. coli_ strains were cultured at 37 °C in LB medium by supplementary of kanamycin (50 µg/mL). When cell OD600 (optical

density at 600 nm) reached 0.60, isopropyl-β-D-thiogalactoside (IPTG) was supplemented into the culture media with an induction content of 0.50 mM. After incubating at 25 °C for 12 h, cells were washed and centrifuged in 50 mM phosphate buffer with pH 7.0 (8000 × g, 8 min), and finally collected and used for bioreduction.

In this study, several bioreaction parameters was tested on the bio-reduction of CFPO. In the reaction system containing potassium phosphate buffer (100 mM, pH 6.0-8.0), CFPO was biologically catalyzed with glucose (0-3.0 mol/mol CFPO), NAD+ (0-3.0 µM/mM CFPO), DESS (HBA: ChCl; HBD: TA, MOA, MA, CA and LA) dosage (0-50, vol%), 100.0 mM CFPO, whole cells (0.1 g/mL), metal ions (Zn2+, Sn4+, Ba2+, Al3+, Ca2+, Mn2+, Cu2+, Mg2+, Ni2+, and Fe2+) (1.0 mM). After incubation in a shaker (180 rpm) for 0-8 h under the temperature of 30 °C, CFPO and (S)-CFPL then detected by HPLC.

The solubility of CFPO was measured at pH 7.0 and 30 °C in DES-water. In the mixture of ChCl:LA (7.5 vol%) and water (92.5 vol%), the solubility of CFPO was 44.2 g/L. In the mixture of ChCl:MA (7.5 vol %) and water (92.5 vol%), the solubility of CFPO was 51.8 g/L. In the mixture of ChCl:CA (7.5 vol%) and water (92.5 vol%), the solubility of CFPO was 38.7 g/L. In the mixture of ChCl:TA (7.5 vol%) and water (92.5 vol%), the solubility of CFPO was 46.3 g/L. In the mixture of ChCl: MOA (7.5 vol%) and water (92.5 vol%), the solubility of CFPO was 30.6 g/L. To test the influence of substrate CFPO concentrations on the stability of reductase. 50–600 mM commercial CFPO, a certain amount of glucose and NAD$^+$, and whole cells (0.1 g/mL, wet weight) were mixed together in the mixture of ChCl:LA (7.5 vol%) and water (92.5 vol%) (pH 7.0) under the temperature of 30 °C for 0–24 h. The production of (S)-CFPL was calculated by extracting samples periodically, extracting the (S)-CFPL produced by ethyl acetate and the unreacted CFPO, and analyzing them using HPLC.

## 2.9. Analytical methods The viscosity of DESs were measured by a rotary viscometer (NDJ-1C, Shanghai FangRui Instrument Co., Ltd) at 25 °C. FT-IR (Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy) was detected on Thermo Scientific Nicolet iS20 (USA) over 4000–500 cm⁻¹. ¹H NMR (H Nuclear Magnetic Resonance) was carried out by Bruker Avance III HD (400 MHz). DES (5 mg) was dissolved in 250 µL DMSO for ¹H NMR detection. The ee value of (S)-CFPL was measured with GC (model 8890; Agilent Technologies Co., Ltd) containing a CP-Chirasil-Dex-CB column (25 m × 0.25 mm, 0.25 µm) with N₂ as the carrier gas. The substrate CFPO and product (S)-CFPL were measured with HPLC (Agilent 1260) with an Athena C18-WP column (4.6 × 250 mm, 5 µm) at 260 nm using acetonitrile/water (80:20, v/v) as the eluent at a flow rate of 0.8 mL per minute. In addition, water could bridge HBA and HBD, and an appropriate amount of water could improve the stability of the DES-H₂O system [48]. The addition of 10.1 wt% water to DES consisting of ChCl and glycerol strengthened the direct hydrogen-bond between ChCl and glycerol [49]. Hence, the different volumetric ratio of ChCl:LA-to-water might greatly affect the biological reduction of CFPO to (S)-CFPL. In DES ChCl:LA-H₂O, the volumetric ratio range of 0–50 v% ChCl:LA was used (Fig. 3b). When the volumetric ratio of ChCl:LA increased from 0 to 7.5 v %, the relative activity gradually increased from 65.2 % to 93.3 %. As the ratio of ChCl:LA increased from 7.5 to 10 v%, the relative activity did not increase apparently. The relative activity was weakened obviously when ChCl:LA was more than 10 v%. Excessive water loading in ChCl: LA-H₂O might cause changes in osmotic pressure of the solution, which not only facilitated contact between reductase and substrates in the whole cells, but also reduced potential product or substrate inhibition, thus enhancing biocatalytic efficiency [50]. Apparently, the optimum dose of ChCl:LA was 7.5 % by volume, and ChCl:LA-water (7.5:92.5, v/v) was used in subsequent investigation. The ee value of (S)-CFPL was detected by GC, reaching over 99 % (Fig. S3 in Supporting Information). The ionization of hydrogen ions in DES might affect the synthesis of small organic molecules, suggesting that the acidity of carboxylic acid groups would affect the production of (S)-CFPL [51]. In the biological of reduction of CFPO, a linear relationship [Y[(S)-CFPL], %] = 32.621 × X(pKa of carboxylic acid) - 34.786, R²=0.9745] was observed between the pKa of

carboxylic acid and the yield of (S)-CFPL (Fig. 3c). The high pKa of carboxylic acid in DES would promote the synthesis of (S)-CFPL. When pKa increased from 2.82 to 3.86, the yield of (S)-CFPL increased linearly, which might be related to the increase of proton utilization rate. High pKa value of HBD, the weaker its acidity, facilitated the whole-cell bioreduction of CFPO. From the structural characteristics of a-carbox- ylic acid of LA, it could be seen that stronger H-bonding formed after, protonation and ion-dipole interaction was established between DES and water, increasing the freedom degree of bioreduction activity and further improving the bioreduction efficiency of the bioreaction system [52].

In the process of biocatalytic reaction, different viscosity of DESs might affect the efficiency of biocatalytic reaction [53]. Therefore, the viscosity of five DES was tested (Fig. 3d). The results indicated that the viscosity of DES (ChCl:LA) was relatively low. High viscosity of DES will cause a great damage degree of cell membrane, leading to a small leakage of material inside the cell membrane, thereby limiting mass transfer [54]. In DES composed of acetamide, urea and sorbitol, the lower the viscosity of the reaction medium, the higher the activity of bromelain [55].
3.3. *Investigation of cells membrane permeability by supplementary of DES*
The cell membrane is the first target of the solvent [56]. When the

cell permeability is enhanced, its components (protein and nucleic acid) can be easily released. The change in the efficiency of whole-cell bio- catalysis suggested a certain interaction between cells and DESs. 3.4. Polarity analysis of DESs The Kamlet-Taft solvatochromic method could be used as a quanti- tative tool to estimate the chemical properties of two component car- boxylic acids DESs. Kamlet-Taft parameters π*, α and β represent the hydrogen-bond dipolarity/polarizability, acidity and basicity of the solvent, respectively [59]. DESs with a high α value could easily provide hydrogen-bonds to liberate H+ and have a high acidity. DESs with a high β value had higher hydrogen-bond acceptance capacity. The α and β values of ChCl:LA were 0.51 and 0.53, respectively, indicating that the acidity and hydrogen-bond acceptability of the solvent were low (Table 2). However, the initial reaction rate in ChCl:LA-H2O system was the highest, reaching 1.52 mM/min. This might be due to the fact that the system had fewer active protons, reduced the acidic site, and made the pH value of the solvent more neutral, which was more suitable for whole-cells to participate in biological reduction.
3.5. Enhancement of biological reduction from CFPO to (S)-CFPL by using the mixture of ChCl:LA and H2O as reaction system

It is well known that bioreaction temperature, medium pH, metal ion additive, co-substrate, and cofactor could influence the bioreduction greatly during the biological transformation [60–62]. Thus, it was necessary to optimize biological reduction factors (such as glucose content, cofactor NAD⁺ loading, metal ion, reaction temperature, reaction pH, etc.) in order to enhance the bioreduction efficiency. The performance temperature and medium pH have a crucial influence on the bioreaction [63]. As displayed in Fig. 6a, the highest CFPO-reducing activity was observed at 30 °C. Beyond this performance temperature, the bioreduction activity declined gradually. When the performance temperature increased, the three-dimensional structure of reductase changed, thus lowering the activity of reductase. When the temperature was too high, the structure of the enzyme molecules would change irreversibly, making the enzyme inactive [64]. The highest reduction activity was observed at pH 7.0 (Fig. 6b). Glucose has been utilized as co-substrate to regenerate intracellular cofactor [66,67]. As displayed in Fig. 6c, by raising glucose load from 0 to 2.0 mol glucose per mol CFPO, the reduction activity increased greatly. Over the loading of 2.0 mol glucose per mol CFPO, the catalytic activity of CFPO was weakened gradually. The addition of excessive glucose would make the bioreaction medium more viscous, thereby

In a bioreduction reaction system, cofactor NAD+ is a common prerequisite for enhancing the biological reduction efficiency [69,70]. The effect of NAD+ dose on CFPO-reducing bioreaction was displayed in Fig. 6d. Upon raising NAD+ content from 0 to 1.5 µm NAD+/mmol CFPO, the relative activity increased gradually. As the content of NAD+ reached 1.5 µm NAD+/mmol CFPO, the biocatalytic activity arrived at the maximum. After NAD+ exceeded 1.5 µm NAD+/mmol CFPO, the activity declined. Thus, the optimal NAD+ load for the biological reduction of CFPO was 1.5 µm NAD+ per mmol CFPO.

In the biocatalytic process, the addition of metal ions might stabilize the structure of intermediate and avoid the occurrence of unwanted side-reactions, thus enhancing productivity [71]. Accordingly, different chloride salts (1.0 mM) were supplemented to ChCl:LA-H2O system at 30 °C and pH 7.0. As revealed in Fig. 6e, Ba2+ and Cu2+ had strong inhibition on the reductase activity. Mg2+, Ca2+, and Zn2+ enhanced the bioreduction activity. In particular, Mg2+ (0.1 mM) gave the highest activity. Effects of Mg2+ doses (0–2.0 mM) were examined on the reductase activity at pH 7.0 under the temperature of 30 °C (Fig. 6f). It was observed that Mg2+ (0.025–2.0 mM) did not inhibit the biological reduction, suggesting that Mg2+ might promote the whole-cell bioconversion of CFPO. The highest biocatalytic activity was detected in the existence of 1.0 mM Mg2+. In the future, in-depth exploration will be conducted on how does the docking affect about reductase and DES components. Furthermore, the cost-effective biosynthesis of (S)-CFPL from the high titer of CFPO with robust reductase would be developed in an eco-friendlier and more sustainable bioreduction system.

4. Conclusion Biocatalysis is currently accepted as a one of key methodologies for manufacturing chiral drug intermediates. In this work, molecular docking revealed that CFPO at the binding site of CmCR had a binding energy of -6.7 kcal/mol, which favored the bioreduction of CFPO. The efficient asymmetric transformation of CFPO to prepare (S)-CFPL was successfully carried out in DES-water system through the whole cells bioreduction with E. coli cell harboring CmCR. It was found that the high pKa value of carboxylic acid (as HBD) in ChCl-based DES and low viscosity of DES might be beneficial to promote the cell membrane permeability of whole-cells and enhance the bioreduction efficiency. In the ChCl:LA-H2O system, 100 mM CFPO was converted to (S)-CFPL with a yield of 95.9 %. This strategy provided a sustainable and efficient biocatalytic method for the effective preparation of (S)-CFPL.

Molecular Catalysis 550 (2023) 113570 <::logo: Elsevier NON SOLLUS An illustration of a person picking fruit from a tree with a banner that reads "NON SOLLUS" and the word "ELSEVIER" below::> Contents lists available at ScienceDirect Molecular Catalysis journal homepage: www.journals.elsevier.com/molecular-catalysis <::logo: Elsevier MOLECULAR CATALYSIS ScienceDirect ISSN 2405-8123 An abstract pattern of interconnected, colorful lines is displayed on a dark blue background.::> <::logo: Unknown Check for updates A red and yellow banner-like symbol is centered within a blue circle, all on a light gray square button.::> Efficient whole-cell biosynthesis of (S)-2-chloro-1-(3,4-difluorophenyl)-ethanol from 2-chloro-1-(3,4-difluoro- phenyl) ethanone in a sustainable reaction system Linghui Kong ¹, Bo Fan ¹, Yu-Cai He * School of Pharmacy & School of Biological and Food Engineering, Changzhou University, Changzhou 213164, China ARTICLE INFO --- Keywords: (S)-2-Chloro-1-(3,4-difluorophenyl)-ethanol 2-Chloro-1-(3,4-difluorophenyl) ethanone Asymmetric bioreduction Reductase Deep eutectic solvent ABSTRACT (S)-2-Chloro-1-(3,4-difluorophenyl)-ethanol [(S)-CFPL] is a key chiral intermediate in the manufacture of Ticagrelor. In this study, deep eutectic solvent (DES) was used as the co-solvent, and several reaction parameters were investigated and characterized. It was observed that supplementary of DES could promote the asymmetric reduction of 2-chloro-1-(3,4-difluorophenyl) ethanone (CFPO) to (S)-CFPL through the biological reduction by recombinant E. coli containing a NADH-dependent reductase CmCR. The high pKa value of carboxylic acid in DES and low viscosity of DES were beneficial to increase cell membrane permeability and enhancement of biocatalytic efficiency. By supplementary of DES ChCl:LA (7.5 vol%) into the bioreaction system, the efficient bioreduction reaction of 100 mM CFPO was achieved via the biocatalysis with whole-cell at 30 °C and pH 7.0, affording (S)-CFPL in 95.9% yield and optical purity > 99 %. The process was environmentally friendly with high biocatalytic productivity and had potential practicability in the mass production of (S)-CFPL. ## 1. Introduction Optically active chiral alcohols have received a lot of attention due to their relatively stable molecular structure and their potential as key building-block in the manufacture of materials, pesticides and various compounds used in pharmaceuticals [1]. For example, (_S_)-1-(2, 6-dichloro-3-fluorophenyl) ethanol is an important intermediate for Crizotinib [2]. Other chiral alcohols are also important intermediates of Duloxetine [3], Aprepitant [4], and Sitagliptin [5], as shown in Fig. 1. Chiral compounds are now synthesized by biocatalysts [6-8]. Compared with chemical catalysis, biocatalysis has the characteristics of high ef- ficiency [9,10], specificity [11,12], gentleness [13] and adjustable ac- tivity [14]. Ticagrelor is a platelet aggregation inhibitor primarily used in acute coronary syndromes [15], and (_S_)-2-chloro-1-(3,4-difluor- ophonyl)-ethanol [(_S_)-CFPL] is a key chiral intermediate for preparing Ticagrelor. The chemical synthesis of (_S_)-CFPL involves the reduction of CFPO in organic solvents by chemocatalysts such as borane-methyl sulfide complex and chiral compounds [16]. Compared with bio- catalysis, traditional chemical reduction methods always involve a va- riety of expensive chiral catalysts and cumbersome post-treatment processes [17]. Therefore, the synthesis method of (_S_)-CFPL needs to be * Corresponding author. E-mail addresses: heyucai2001@163.com, yucaihe@cczu.edu.cn (Y.-C. All rights reserved. further improved. Currently, two methods to synthesize chiral alcohols are commonly utilized via biocatalytic approach: dynamic kinetic res- olution and asymmetric bioreduction [18]. Han et al. identified an alcohol dehydrogenase from _Rhodococcus_ R6 that catalyzed the asym- metric transformation of 2-hydroxyacetophenone into (_R_)-(-)-1-phenyl-1,2-ethanediol [19]. Xia et al. obtained three optical compounds by developing a lipase from _Candida Antarctica_ that cata- lyzed the doubly enantioselective ring-opening decomposition between racemic alcohol and lactone [20]. Tozlu et al. used _Lactobacillus para-_ _casei_ BD101 as a biocatalyst for asymmetric reduction of (4-chlor- ophenyl)(phenyl) methane [21]. Chemical catalyst can cause major ecological problems in terms of high energy consumption and toxic waste formation. Biocatalysis has outstanding advantages over chemo- catalysis, including mild reaction conditions, high stereoselectivity and high catalytic efficiency [22]. Biocatalyst is one of the attractive tech- nology options to overcome the limitations of traditional catalysts in this field. During the process of biocatalysis, reaction medium is very impor- tant to improve the biocatalytic efficiency [23]. More and more atten- tion has recently been paid to deep eutectic-solvents (DESs) in biocatalysis [24–26]. DES is commonly composed of L. Kong et al. Molecular Catalysis 550 (2023) 113570 hydrogen-bond-donor (HBD) and hydrogen-bond-acceptor (HBA). Due to its good biocompatibility and high stability, it is considered as the most promising green solvent to replace ionic liquid and organic solvent [27]. DES synthesized from choline chloride is one of the many types of DESs, which could change the composition by adjusting different HBDs [28,29]. DESs have been widely utilized in the chemocatalysis and biocatalysis [30]. They have important physical properties such as viscosity, conductivity, and thermal stability [31–33]. In addition, the typical characteristics of DES in the process of biocatalytic reaction are as follows: (a) higher solubility for substrates with poor water solubility, which make the substrates more easily recognized and utilized by biocatalysts [34]; (b) improve the activity and stability of biocatalysts [35]; (c) reduce the occurrence of side reactions, which make the reaction more selective enantiomers [36]. DES may alter the viscosity of bioreaction medium, and the change in osmolality caused by the viscosity will influence the permeability of cell membrane. The enhanced permeability of bacterial cell membranes (by mutations in its structure) might lead to a significant improvement in whole-cell biocatalytic efficiency [37]. Distinct from the isolated enzymes, one of the main advantages of the whole-cell biocatalysts is that the whole cells provide an excellent natural environment for the enzymes, allow co-factors to regenerate, and avoid enzyme inactivation and denaturation that might occur under some harsh performance conditions [38–41]. The whole cell catalyst is also the cheapest catalyst formulation. DES is a new type of green, solvent with low volatility, high stability, good biocompatibility and other characteristics [33]. In this study, whole cells of recombinant E. coli containing a NADH-dependent reductase CmCR [42] were used for bioreduction of CFPO into (S)-CFPL by using the mixture of DES and H2O as reaction system. The relationship of pKa value of carboxylic acid in DES, viscosity of DES and biocatalytic activity was explored. The effects of DES as a co-solvent on cell viability and cell membrane permeability were also studied, and then the effects of DES on biotransformation were also examined. In addition, biological reaction parameters (such as reaction temperature, pH, co-substrate loading, cofactor loading, metal ion loading and biocatalyst loading) were investigated. Finally, a sustainable production strategy for biocatalytic synthesis of ticagrelor chiral intermediates (S)-CFPL was developed in a benign reaction system. ## 2. Materials and methods ### 2.1. Chemicals and materials CFPO was obtained from Aladdin Co., Ltd. (Shanghai, China). Choline chloride (ChCl), tartaric acid, malonic acid, citric acid, D,L- malic acid, lactic acid, D-glucose, KH2PO4, K2HPO4, MgCl2, and other reagents were from Shanghai Lingfeng Chemical Reagent Co., Ltd. (China). 2.2. _Synthesis of DESs_ Equal molar of ChCl as HBA and organic acid (tartaric acid, malonic acid, citric acid, malic acid, and lactic acid) as HBD were supplemented to a 250-mL flask by stirring magnetically in an oil bath at 80 °C and heated for 2 h. ChCl:Tartaric acid (ChCl:TA), ChCl:Malonic acid (ChCl: MOA), ChCl:Citric acid (ChCl:CA), ChCl: Malic acid (ChCl:MA) and ChCl:Lactic acid (ChCl:LA), were used as cosolvent. 2.3. Determination of Kamlet-Taft parameters of DESs The measurement of Kamlet-Taft (K-T) parameters were determined, with N,N-dimethyl-4-nitroaniline as indices of π*, Nile red dye and 4-nitroaniline as indices of α and β, respectively. Dyes were prepared from anhydrous methanol solution, in which the concentrations of N,N-dimethyl-4-nitrobenzene, Nile red and 4-nitroaniline were all 1 mM. Conclusion Biocatalysis is currently accepted as a one of key methodologies for manufacturing chiral drug intermediates. In this work, molecular docking revealed that CFPO at the binding site of CmCR had a binding energy of -6.7 kcal/mol, which favored the bioreduction of CFPO. The efficient asymmetric transformation of CFPO to prepare (S)-CFPL was successfully carried out in DES-water system through the whole cells bioreduction with E. coli cell harboring CmCR. It was found that the high pKa value of carboxylic acid (as HBD) in ChCl-based DES and low viscosity of DES might be beneficial to promote the cell membrane permeability of whole-cells and enhance the bioreduction efficiency. In the ChCl:LA-H2O system, 100 mM CFPO was converted to (S)-CFPL with a yield of 95.9 %. This strategy provided a sustainable and efficient biocatalytic method for the effective preparation of (S)-CFPL. Molecular Catalysis 550 (2023) 113570 <::logo: Elsevier NON SOLLUS An illustration of a person picking fruit from a tree with a banner that reads "NON SOLLUS" and the word "ELSEVIER" below::> Contents lists available at ScienceDirect Molecular Catalysis journal homepage: www.journals.elsevier.com/molecular-catalysis <::logo: Elsevier MOLECULAR CATALYSIS ScienceDirect ISSN 2405-8123 An abstract pattern of interconnected, colorful lines is displayed on a dark blue background.::> <::logo: Unknown Check for updates A red and yellow banner-like symbol is centered within a blue circle, all on a light gray square button.::> Efficient whole-cell biosynthesis of (S)-2-chloro-1-(3,4-difluorophenyl)-ethanol from 2-chloro-1-(3,4-difluoro- phenyl) ethanone in a sustainable reaction system Linghui Kong ¹, Bo Fan ¹, Yu-Cai He * School of Pharmacy & School of Biological and Food Engineering, Changzhou University, Changzhou 213164, China ARTICLE INFO --- Keywords: (S)-2-Chloro-1-(3,4-difluorophenyl)-ethanol 2-Chloro-1-(3,4-difluorophenyl) ethanone Asymmetric bioreduction Reductase Deep eutectic solvent ABSTRACT (S)-2-Chloro-1-(3,4-difluorophenyl)-ethanol [(S)-CFPL] is a key chiral intermediate in the manufacture of Ticagrelor. In this study, deep eutectic solvent (DES) was used as the co-solvent, and several reaction parameters were investigated and characterized. It was observed that supplementary of DES could promote the asymmetric reduction of 2-chloro-1-(3,4-difluorophenyl) ethanone (CFPO) to (S)-CFPL through the biological reduction by recombinant E. coli containing a NADH-dependent reductase CmCR. The high pKa value of carboxylic acid in DES and low viscosity of DES were beneficial to increase cell membrane permeability and enhancement of biocatalytic efficiency. By supplementary of DES ChCl:LA (7.5 vol%) into the bioreaction system, the efficient bioreduction reaction of 100 mM CFPO was achieved via the biocatalysis with whole-cell at 30 °C and pH 7.0, affording (S)-CFPL in 95.9% yield and optical purity > 99 %. The process was environmentally friendly with high biocatalytic productivity and had potential practicability in the mass production of (S)-CFPL. ## 1. Introduction Optically active chiral alcohols have received a lot of attention due to their relatively stable molecular structure and their potential as key building-block in the manufacture of materials, pesticides and various compounds used in pharmaceuticals [1]. For example, (_S_)-1-(2, 6-dichloro-3-fluorophenyl) ethanol is an important intermediate for Crizotinib [2]. Other chiral alcohols are also important intermediates of Duloxetine [3], Aprepitant [4], and Sitagliptin [5], as shown in Fig. 1. Chiral compounds are now synthesized by biocatalysts [6-8]. Compared with chemical catalysis, biocatalysis has the characteristics of high ef- ficiency [9,10], specificity [11,12], gentleness [13] and adjustable ac- tivity [14]. Ticagrelor is a platelet aggregation inhibitor primarily used in acute coronary syndromes [15], and (_S_)-2-chloro-1-(3,4-difluor- ophonyl)-ethanol [(_S_)-CFPL] is a key chiral intermediate for preparing Ticagrelor. The chemical synthesis of (_S_)-CFPL involves the reduction of CFPO in organic solvents by chemocatalysts such as borane-methyl sulfide complex and chiral compounds [16]. Compared with bio- catalysis, traditional chemical reduction methods always involve a va- riety of expensive chiral catalysts and cumbersome post-treatment processes [17]. Therefore, the synthesis method of (_S_)-CFPL needs to be * Corresponding author. E-mail addresses: heyucai2001@163.com, yucaihe@cczu.edu.cn (Y.-C. All rights reserved. further improved. Currently, two methods to synthesize chiral alcohols are commonly utilized via biocatalytic approach: dynamic kinetic res- olution and asymmetric bioreduction [18]. Han et al. identified an alcohol dehydrogenase from _Rhodococcus_ R6 that catalyzed the asym- metric transformation of 2-hydroxyacetophenone into (_R_)-(-)-1-phenyl-1,2-ethanediol [19]. Xia et al. obtained three optical compounds by developing a lipase from _Candida Antarctica_ that cata- lyzed the doubly enantioselective ring-opening decomposition between racemic alcohol and lactone [20]. Tozlu et al. used _Lactobacillus para-_ _casei_ BD101 as a biocatalyst for asymmetric reduction of (4-chlor- ophenyl)(phenyl) methane [21]. Chemical catalyst can cause major ecological problems in terms of high energy consumption and toxic waste formation. Biocatalysis has outstanding advantages over chemo- catalysis, including mild reaction conditions, high stereoselectivity and high catalytic efficiency [22]. Biocatalyst is one of the attractive tech- nology options to overcome the limitations of traditional catalysts in this field. During the process of biocatalysis, reaction medium is very impor- tant to improve the biocatalytic efficiency [23]. More and more atten- tion has recently been paid to deep eutectic-solvents (DESs) in biocatalysis [24–26]. DES is commonly composed of L. Kong et al. Molecular Catalysis 550 (2023) 113570 hydrogen-bond-donor (HBD) and hydrogen-bond-acceptor (HBA). Due to its good biocompatibility and high stability, it is considered as the most promising green solvent to replace ionic liquid and organic solvent [27]. DES synthesized from choline chloride is one of the many types of DESs, which could change the composition by adjusting different HBDs [28,29]. DESs have been widely utilized in the chemocatalysis and biocatalysis [30]. They have important physical properties such as viscosity, conductivity, and thermal stability [31–33]. In addition, the typical characteristics of DES in the process of biocatalytic reaction are as follows: (a) higher solubility for substrates with poor water solubility, which make the substrates more easily recognized and utilized by biocatalysts [34]; (b) improve the activity and stability of biocatalysts [35]; (c) reduce the occurrence of side reactions, which make the reaction more selective enantiomers [36]. DES may alter the viscosity of bioreaction medium, and the change in osmolality caused by the viscosity will influence the permeability of cell membrane. The enhanced permeability of bacterial cell membranes (by mutations in its structure) might lead to a significant improvement in whole-cell biocatalytic efficiency [37]. Distinct from the isolated enzymes, one of the main advantages of the whole-cell biocatalysts is that the whole cells provide an excellent natural environment for the enzymes, allow co-factors to regenerate, and avoid enzyme inactivation and denaturation that might occur under some harsh performance conditions [38–41]. The whole cell catalyst is also the cheapest catalyst formulation. DES is a new type of green, solvent with low volatility, high stability, good biocompatibility and other characteristics [33]. In this study, whole cells of recombinant E. coli containing a NADH-dependent reductase CmCR [42] were used for bioreduction of CFPO into (S)-CFPL by using the mixture of DES and H2O as reaction system. The relationship of pKa value of carboxylic acid in DES, viscosity of DES and biocatalytic activity was explored. The effects of DES as a co-solvent on cell viability and cell membrane permeability were also studied, and then the effects of DES on biotransformation were also examined. In addition, biological reaction parameters (such as reaction temperature, pH, co-substrate loading, cofactor loading, metal ion loading and biocatalyst loading) were investigated. Finally, a sustainable production strategy for biocatalytic synthesis of ticagrelor chiral intermediates (S)-CFPL was developed in a benign reaction system. ## 2. Materials and methods ### 2.1. Chemicals and materials CFPO was obtained from Aladdin Co., Ltd. (Shanghai, China). Kamlet-Taft parameters π*, α and β represent the hydrogen-bond dipolarity/polarizability, acidity and basicity of the solvent, respectively [59]. Conclusion Biocatalysis is currently accepted as a one of key methodologies for manufacturing chiral drug intermediates. In this work, molecular docking revealed that CFPO at the binding site of CmCR had a binding energy of -6.7 kcal/mol, which favored the bioreduction of CFPO. The efficient asymmetric transformation of CFPO to prepare (S)-CFPL was successfully carried out in DES-water system through the whole cells bioreduction with E. coli cell harboring CmCR. It was found that the high pKa value of carboxylic acid (as HBD) in ChCl-based DES and low viscosity of DES might be beneficial to promote the cell membrane permeability of whole-cells and enhance the bioreduction efficiency. In the ChCl:LA-H2O system, 100 mM CFPO was converted to (S)-CFPL with a yield of 95.9 %. This strategy provided a sustainable and efficient biocatalytic method for the effective preparation of (S)-CFPL.
